title: NEB Class 12 Biology — Environmental Issues — 2024
subject: biology
source: NEB Grade 12 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Explain the greenhouse effect and global warming, naming the main greenhouse gases and their major sources.
questions.solution:
**Greenhouse effect:** the atmosphere transmits incoming short-wave solar radiation but traps the longer-wave infrared radiation re-emitted by the earth, keeping the surface warm. It is natural and essential — without it the earth would average about −18 °C instead of +15 °C.

**Global warming** is the enhancement of this effect by added greenhouse gases: **carbon dioxide** (fossil-fuel burning, deforestation), **methane** (paddy fields, cattle, landfills), **chlorofluorocarbons**, **nitrous oxide** (fertilisers) and water vapour. Their rising concentration tilts the radiation balance so more heat is retained.

**Consequences:** melting glaciers and rising sea level, erratic monsoon and more extreme weather, coral bleaching, shifts in the range of species and crop belts, and threat to island nations.
questions.knowledgeNote: CO₂ contributes most of the warming because of its abundance, even though methane is a far stronger absorber molecule for molecule.

questions.question: What is ozone depletion? Explain its mechanism by chlorofluorocarbons and state the international response.
questions.solution:
**Ozone depletion** is the thinning of the stratospheric ozone layer that filters harmful ultraviolet rays.

**Mechanism:** chlorofluorocarbons released from refrigerants, aerosol propellants and foam-blowing agents are stable in the troposphere and drift up. In the stratosphere UV light splits them, releasing **chlorine free radicals**, which catalytically destroy ozone:

Cl + O₃ → ClO + O₂, then ClO + O → Cl + O₂ — the chlorine is regenerated, so a single atom destroys thousands of ozone molecules. The process is fastest in the polar stratospheric clouds of Antarctica, producing the ozone hole.

**Response:** the **Montreal Protocol (1987)** phased out CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances; the layer is slowly recovering.
questions.knowledgeNote: Ozone depletion is not the same as the greenhouse effect: ozone filters UV, while greenhouse gases trap infrared — do not conflate the two in answers.

questions.question: Define biochemical oxygen demand and explain what a high BOD indicates about water quality. Why does sewage discharge raise the BOD of a river?
questions.solution:
**BOD (biochemical oxygen demand)** is the amount of dissolved oxygen consumed by microorganisms in oxidising the organic matter present in a unit volume of water, measured over 5 days at 20 °C and expressed in mg L⁻¹ (ppm).

A **high BOD** means a large amount of biodegradable organic waste, so the water is polluted; clean water has a BOD below about 5 ppm.

**Sewage discharge** adds organic matter, so aerobic bacteria multiply and consume the dissolved oxygen, raising the BOD. When BOD becomes very high, oxygen falls so low that fish die and anaerobic decomposition sets in, producing foul-smelling gases — the river loses its capacity to support life.
questions.knowledgeNote: High BOD also signals eutrophication risk: the nutrients in sewage and fertiliser run-off feed algal blooms which further deplete oxygen when they decay.
